```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
source("helpers/report_widgets.R")

read_result <- function(name, optional = FALSE) {
  path <- file.path(params$results_dir, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  if (file.exists(path)) return(readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE))
  if (!optional) stop("Missing ", path, ". Run Script_4_reporting.R first.")
}

site <- read_result("site_summary")
field <- read_result("field_stock_summary")
cores <- read_result("core_stocks")
checks <- read_result("section_checks")
coverage <- read_result("mapping_coverage")
ecosystems <- read_result("janousek_ecosystems")
estuaries <- read_result("janousek_estuary_comparison", optional = TRUE)
totals <- read_result("mapping_totals")
transfer <- read_result("transfer_summary", optional = TRUE)
transfer_maps <- read_result("transfer_interactive_maps", optional = TRUE)
maps <- read_result("interactive_maps", optional = TRUE)
prior <- read_result("bayesian_prior_parameters", optional = TRUE)
settings <- read_result("mapping_settings", optional = TRUE)

depth_label <- function(depth) paste0("0–", depth, " cm")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2L) {
  ifelse(is.finite(x), formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f", big.mark = ","), "—")
}
report_table <- function(data, caption) {
  knitr::kable(data, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE, format = "pipe")
}
report_figure <- function(filename, folder = params$results_dir) {
  knitr::include_graphics(file.path(folder, filename))
}

all_cores <- field |> filter(zone == "All cores") |> arrange(depth_cm)
deepest <- all_cores |> filter(complete > 0) |> slice_max(depth_cm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
simulated <- grepl("simulat", site$data_source, ignore.case = TRUE)
unclassified <- cores |> filter(is.na(habitat) | habitat == "Unclassified") |>
  summarise(n = n_distinct(`Core ID`)) |> pull(n)


```

## Summary

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (simulated) {
  cat("::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n## Workshop example\n",
      "This workshop uses simulated core values. The stock estimates and maps are examples for practice.\n",
      ":::\n", sep = "")
}
```

The study includes **`r fmt(site$logged_cores, 0)` cores** from `r fmt(site$plots, 0)` plots in `r fmt(site$zones, 0)` zones. The study area covers **`r fmt(site$area_ha, 0)` ha**. For the `r depth_label(deepest$depth_cm)` estimate, the median stock across `r fmt(deepest$complete, 0)` usable cores was **`r fmt(deepest$median_kg_m2)` kg C/m²**.

```{r}
report_table(all_cores |>
  transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), `Cores used` = complete, `Shorter cores` = short_cores,
            Mean = fmt(mean_kg_m2), SD = fmt(sd_kg_m2), Median = fmt(median_kg_m2),
            Range = if_else(complete > 0, paste0(fmt(min_kg_m2), " to ", fmt(max_kg_m2)), "—")),
  "Carbon stock by depth (kg C/m²). Shorter cores contribute stock to their sampled bottom. Standard deviation (SD) shows how much stock varies among cores.")
```

## Data and methods

We used `r fmt(site$sections, 0)` sediment sections. For cores that shortened during sampling, we scaled the depths by the ratio of the length inserted to the length recovered. We assumed each core compressed evenly. We used dry sediment mass and organic carbon content to calculate stock for each section.

For 0–30 cm, we add the carbon from the surface down to 30 cm or the sampled bottom, whichever comes first. If a section crosses 30 cm, we divide its stock by its thickness in centimetres and multiply by the centimetres inside the 0–30 cm interval. We use the same rule for 50 and 100 cm.

We treat the sampled bottom of a usable short core as the maximum depth and carry its sampled stock forward to deeper targets. A 20 cm core therefore gives the same stock at all three targets. A 40 cm core gives its stock to 30 cm for the first target and its stock to 40 cm for both deeper targets. An unusable section or a gap prevents us from estimating stock beyond that break.

```{r}
report_table(checks |>
  transmute(`Carbon method` = coalesce(carbon_method, "Unavailable"),
            `Section check` = coalesce(section_check, "Unavailable"),
            `Lab review` = coalesce(lab_review, "—"), Sections = sections),
  paste("Section checks.", fmt(site$cores_to_review, 0), "cores were flagged for review."))
```

## Comparison with Janousek cores

We compared the study cores with cores from Janousek et al. (2025) in Alaska, British Columbia, Washington and Oregon. The reference values come from Janousek cores that reached the stated depth. Study cores contribute stock to the stated depth or to their sampled bottom.

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (unclassified > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Habitat is unknown for %s of %s study cores. The figures show how those cores compare with regional and B.C. salt-marsh data.\n",
              fmt(unclassified, 0), fmt(site$logged_cores, 0)))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reference-profiles
#| fig-cap: "Study zone averages and Janousek salt-marsh ranges by depth. Shaded bands show the middle 50% and 80% of reference values."
#| fig-alt: "Coloured lines show study zone averages against grey ranges from Janousek cores."
report_figure("janousek_profiles.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reference-ecosystems

report_figure("carbon_stock_context.png", params$field_dir)
```

British Columbia and Pacific Northwest comparisons remain visible for each depth. Choose an estuary to add it to the graph and table. The Pacific Northwest group includes British Columbia. A selected estuary appears at the depths reached by its reference cores.

```{r}
#| label: estuary-comparison
if (is.null(estuaries)) {

```

## Explore the maps

Choose a depth and use the layer menu to compare each stock estimate with its uncertainty. **CV** is the coefficient of variation, calculated at each cell as SD divided by mean stock. A CV of 0.5 means the SD is half the mean. Estimates and SD use kg C/m². Cells with a missing SD or a nonpositive estimate have no CV. Pooled and zone CV layers use variability among sampled plots. IDW uses an SD estimated from held-out residuals. Click a cell to read its value. The satellite background loads online.

```{r}
report_map_picker(maps, params$results_dir, "sediment carbon")
```

## Stock across the study boundary

These maps use cells `r fmt(site$grid_spacing_m, 0)` m apart. The pooled estimate averages the sampled plots. The zone-weighted estimate uses each zone's average stock and area. Inverse distance weighting (IDW) gives more weight to nearby cores. The local Matérn model also uses distance to estimate stock across the grid. The Bayesian model updates a starting estimate from Janousek cores with the study cores.

```{r}
report_table(coverage |> arrange(depth_cm) |>
  transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), `Mapped cores` = mapped_cores,
            `Mapped plots` = mapped_plots, `Cores without a usable estimate` = incomplete_or_invalid_cores),
  "Core and plot coverage at each mapping depth.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapping-totals
#| fig-cap: "Total carbon by method and depth. Bars show one standard error or standard deviation, as labelled."
#| fig-alt: "Points show total stock estimates by method and depth. Bars show uncertainty where available."
report_figure("mapping_totals.png")
```

```{r}
report_table(totals |> arrange(depth_cm) |>
  transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), Method = method,
            `Mean stock (kg C/m²)` = fmt(mean_kg_c_m2), `Total (Mg C)` = fmt(total_mg_c, 0),
            `Coverage (%)` = fmt(coverage_pct, 0),
            `Uncertainty (Mg C)` = if_else(is.finite(uncertainty_mg_c),
              paste0("±", fmt(uncertainty_mg_c, 0), " ", uncertainty_type), "—")),
  "Estimated sediment carbon stocks by depth and method.")
```

The sampling standard error (SE) shows how much an estimate could vary with a different sample of plots. The model SD for a total accounts for how estimates at nearby locations vary together. A dash marks an unavailable value.

## Transfer Learning with embeddings kernel

AlphaEarth describes each map cell with 64 values called embeddings. The embeddings kernel gives more weight to Janousek cores from places with similar values. This gives a starting estimate called the Janousek prior. The local Matérn model adjusts that estimate using the study cores and their distance from each cell.

```{r}
#| label: transfer-results
#| results: asis
if (is.null(transfer) || !nrow(transfer)) {
  cat("Run Scripts 3 and 4 to populate the transfer results.\n")
} else {
  transfer_rows <- transfer |> arrange(depth_cm, desc(surface))
  print(report_table(transfer_rows |>
    transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), Surface = tools::toTitleCase(surface),
              `Janousek cores` = fmt(n_reference_cores, 0),
              `Local cores used` = if_else(surface == "posterior", fmt(n_local_cores_used, 0), "—"),
              `Coverage (%)` = fmt(100 * coverage_fraction, 1),
              `Mean stock (kg C/m²)` = fmt(mean_covered_kg_c_m2),
              `AOI stock (Mg C)` = fmt(aoi_stock_Mg_C, 0)),
    "Transfer stock by depth. The mean accounts for the area of each cell with an estimate."))
  cat("\n\n")
  if ("area_weighted_cv" %in% names(transfer_rows)) {
    print(report_table(transfer_rows |>
      transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), Surface = tools::toTitleCase(surface),
                `Cells with CV` = fmt(cells_with_cv, 0),
                `Area-weighted CV` = fmt(area_weighted_cv),
                `CV range` = if_else(is.finite(min_cv) & is.finite(max_cv),
                                      paste(fmt(min_cv), "to", fmt(max_cv)), "—")),
      "Relative uncertainty by depth. CV is point SD divided by the corresponding estimate."))
  }
}
```

### Transfer estimates and uncertainty maps

Choose a depth and use the **Map layer** dropdown. **AlphaEarth embeddings** shows three of the embedding values as colours. **Janousek prior** shows the starting stock estimate. **Local Matérn correction** shows the updated stock estimate minus that starting estimate. Use **Prior uncertainty (CV)** and **Updated uncertainty (CV)** to compare relative uncertainty before and after adding local data. The corresponding SD layers show absolute uncertainty in kg C/m².

```{r}
#| label: transfer-maps
report_map_picker(transfer_maps, params$results_dir, "transfer learning")
```

## Interpretation and limitations

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!is.null(settings)) {
  model_check <- settings |> filter(is.finite(rmse_log)) |> group_by(depth_cm) |>
    slice_min(rmse_log, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()
  if (nrow(model_check) > 0 && n_distinct(model_check$method) == 1) {
    cat(sprintf("Among the local models, **%s** had the smallest prediction error at all %s depths tested. We checked this by leaving plots out of the fit and predicting their stocks on the log scale.\n\n",
                first(model_check$method), fmt(nrow(model_check), 0)))
  }
}
if (!is.null(prior) && any(totals$method == "Bayesian posterior")) {
  fitted <- prior |> filter(status == "Fitted") |> arrange(depth_cm)
  if (nrow(fitted)) {
    habitat <- paste(unique(fitted$ecosystem), collapse = ", ")
    cat(sprintf("The Bayesian model used **%s** cores for its starting estimate. Confirm the local habitat before using that estimate for the site.\n\n",
                tolower(habitat)))
  }
}
```

Each total uses stock up to the listed depth or the sampled bottom at each study core. The totals overlap across depths. Estimates vary with the reference cores, the sampling coverage and the mapping method.

## Reference

Janousek, C. N., et al. (2025). Blue carbon stocks along the Pacific coast of North America are mainly driven by local rather than regional factors. *Global Biogeochemical Cycles, 39*, e2024GB008239. [doi:10.1029/2024GB008239](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024GB008239)

## Monitoring, reporting, and verification

```{r}
#| label: mrv-and-sampling-plan
#| results: asis
mrv_dir <- "outputs/script5_mrv"
mrv_files <- c(statistics = "mrv_statistics.csv", validation = "model_validation.csv",
               zones = "zone_guidance.csv", plan = "monitoring_plan.csv",
               actions = "next_steps.csv")
mrv_paths <- file.path(mrv_dir, mrv_files)

if (!all(file.exists(mrv_paths))) {
  cat("Run `Script_5_MRV.R` after Scripts 1 and 2 to generate the baseline statistics, maps, and sampling plan.\n")
} else {
  mrv <- lapply(setNames(mrv_paths, names(mrv_files)), readr::read_csv,
                show_col_types = FALSE)
  mrv_depth <- mrv$plan$depth_cm[[1L]]

  cat("### Baseline carbon stock\n\n")
  if (simulated) cat("The workshop uses simulated cores. These estimates illustrate the workflow.\n\n")
  cat("The results describe baseline sediment carbon stocks. Estimating change and net removals requires a repeat campaign and the applicable blue carbon methodology.\n\n")
  print(report_table(mrv$statistics |>
    transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), Model = coalesce(model, "Unavailable"),
              `Cores reaching depth` = full_depth_cores, `Usable plots` = full_depth_qc_mapped_plots,
              `Map coverage (%)` = fmt(coverage_pct, 1),
              `Mapped mean (Mg C/ha)` = fmt(covered_mean_mg_c_ha, 1),
              `AOI stock (Mg C)` = fmt(aoi_stock_mg_c, 0),
              `AOI stock SD (Mg C)` = fmt(aoi_stock_sd_mg_c, 0)),
    "Area-weighted baseline estimates. A dash indicates an unavailable value."))
  if (any(!is.finite(mrv$statistics$aoi_stock_sd_mg_c))) {
    cat("\n\nWhere project-wide stock uncertainty is unavailable, the point-level standard deviation (SD) cannot substitute for it.\n")
  }

  cat("\n\n### Stock, uncertainty, and sampling gaps\n\n",
      "White circles mark usable cores. Yellow diamonds mark areas to inspect before drawing new samples. Use distance from usable cores to identify gaps in coverage, particularly when the selected IDW model has constant CV.\n\n", sep = "")
  mrv_map_depths <- c(mrv_depth, setdiff(mrv$statistics$depth_cm, mrv_depth))
  mrv_maps <- file.path(mrv_dir, paste0("mrv_", mrv_map_depths, "cm.png"))
  mrv_map_exists <- file.exists(mrv_maps)
  if (any(mrv_map_exists)) {
    cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
    for (i in which(mrv_map_exists)) {
      cat(sprintf("#### %s\n\n![Mapped stock, uncertainty CV, and distance to usable cores at %s.](%s){width=100%%}\n\n",
                  depth_label(mrv_map_depths[i]), depth_label(mrv_map_depths[i]), mrv_maps[i]))
    }
    cat(":::\n\n")
  }

  cat("### Where to sample next\n\n")
  print(report_table(mrv$zones |> filter(depth_cm == mrv_depth) |> arrange(priority_order) |>
    transmute(Priority = priority_order, Zone = zone, `Usable plots` = full_depth_qc_plots,
              `Largest gap (km)` = fmt(max_gap_m / 1000, 1), Action = action),
    paste("Sampling priorities at", depth_label(mrv_depth), "in recommended order.")))

  cat("\n\n### When to repeat sampling\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("The planning calculation uses %.0f%% confidence and %.0f%% power for independent paired plots.\n\n",
              100 * mrv$plan$confidence, 100 * mrv$plan$power))
  if (is.finite(mrv$plan$minimum_detectable_change_mg_c_ha)) {
    cat(sprintf("The planned repeat panel has an approximate minimum detectable change of %s Mg C/ha.\n\n",
                fmt(mrv$plan$minimum_detectable_change_mg_c_ha)))
  }
  cat(paste(sprintf("%d. %s", mrv$actions$order, mrv$actions$action), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n", sep = "")

  if (nrow(mrv$validation)) {
    cat("### Model checks\n\n")
    print(report_table(mrv$validation |>
      transmute(Depth = depth_label(depth_cm), Model = method, Selected = if_else(selected, "Yes", ""),
                `Held-out plots` = held_out_plots, `Log RMSE` = fmt(rmse_log, 3),
                `RMSE (Mg C/ha)` = fmt(rmse_mg_c_ha), `Bias (Mg C/ha)` = fmt(bias_mg_c_ha)),
      "Held-out performance on common plots. RMSE is the root mean square error."))
    cat("\n\nThe same folds were used for model tuning, so the scores are exploratory. The Bayesian and AlphaEarth transfer surfaces lack comparable held-out scores.\n\n")
  }
  cat("[Standalone MRV report](outputs/script5_mrv/mrv_report.html) · [Sampling areas for GIS](outputs/script5_mrv/sampling_guidance.gpkg)\n")
}
```
